candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Hymns on the Crucifixion
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Hymns on the Crucifixion IX.2-4 (NPNF S2 V13). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Hymns on the Crucifixion (c. 365 AD)

The rock struck by Moses' rod pours out water for the thirsty people, and Ephrem joins Paul (1 Cor 10:4) in reading the rock as Christ. The striking is the Crucifixion; the water is the Spirit and the eucharistic stream (Jn 19:34 — blood and water from the pierced side). Tewahedo treats Ex 17:6 and Jn 19:34 as a single canonical disclosure of the smitten Christ releasing the rivers of living water.

candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Exodus
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus XVII.5 (NPNF S2 V13, Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

When Moses lifted up his hands Israel prevailed against Amalek; when he let them down Amalek prevailed. Ephrem reads the cruciform posture as the secret of the victory: Moses' arms outstretched are the Cross fore-figured, and the war is won not by the sword in the valley but by the cross-shape on the hill. Tewahedo carries this as the canonical OT type of Christian intercessory prayer in the cross-posture.
